You are entirely correct. Matt Pocock is still a nice guy with reasonable opinions and shares a lot with us. I've personally learned from reading his skills.
Skills are hardly transferrable unless focusing on globally applicable things. The most useful skills are project/organization-specific 'tribal knowledge' — not public skill sets like this.

If I had a nickel for every dev who has written a 'productivity suite' of skills and shared it as a burst of innovation ... when it's really extremely specific to that dev and their workflow, I'd have a lot of nickels.

All this could be one moderately-sized AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md. If you're detailing something like TDD in such detail, you're probably hampering the model with a definition less accurate than what it learned in training.
The second skill example claims 'materialization cascade' is easier reading than the plain-English before version — is it just me, or does anyone else prefer the first (plain) version?

Matt Pocock has a hand-wavy approach to engineering in a silo, then uses that output as a foundation for tools while touting them as best practice on YouTube; the prose in his skill files often has very little utility, wrapped in a ball of wax.
Christ, this is exhausting.
